key_insight: SayWhen enables early speech by releasing a task-directed act shared across plausible continuation plans and vetoing playback if new transcripts invalidate it.
engineering_relevance: Voice agents can reduce response latency by controlling supported public commitments rather than simply predicting and speaking the most likely response.
method: Identify a shared task-directed act across typed continuation plans.
Control speech release with a persistent transcript-based veto.
Measure regret-free early speech (RFES): supported pre-endpoint releases without scored incompatibility.
evidence_signal: On 72 branching prefixes, generated plans achieved 6.0% RFES with zero observed mean regret versus 8.2% and 0.068 for Matched Top-One; separately, schema-derived candidates with cached TTS achieved task-level RFES on 21/30 simulated voice tasks.
watch_item: Planner latency limits generated-plan deployment, while schema-based results rely on predefined structure and cached TTS in a small simulation.
paper_title: SayWhen: Set-Valued Semantic Commitment for Low-Regret Early Speech
